title: Lunar gravity is about a sixth of terrestrial gravity
summary: Because the Moon has less mass, its gravitational pull is about one-sixth of Earth's, and a jump goes about six times higher.
body: On the same NASA Science questions page, the comparison is a fraction. Less lunar mass means a weaker tug, about one-sixth of the tug at home. The page adds that a person could jump about six times as high and would land again. Updated 12 February 2026. This is the plain fraction and the jump, not a fact-sheet row in metres per second squared.
